error.signature: AI tells someone in Pakistan they must get a doctor's prescription before any pharmacy will sell them antibiotics

verdict.summary: Under the Drugs Act 1976, antibiotics in Pakistan are legally prescription-only, and Pakistan's drug regulator DRAP reaffirmed in 2024 that pharmacies must not dispense them without a registered doctor's prescription. In practice, enforcement is inconsistent — peer-reviewed surveys of Pakistani pharmacies found a substantial share of antibiotics are still dispensed without any prescription, on patient request or pharmacist recommendation. Assuming the law is strictly enforced everywhere is wrong; so is assuming self-purchased antibiotics are medically safe just because they're available.

dead_ends.action: Assume every pharmacy in Pakistan will refuse to sell antibiotics without a doctor's prescription, and delay treatment to first arrange a doctor visit
dead_ends.why_fails: While the Drugs Act 1976 makes antibiotics prescription-only and DRAP issued a nationwide advisory in August 2024 restating this, a peer-reviewed dispensing-pattern study of pharmacies in Islamabad and Rawalpindi found 35.2% of antibiotics were handed out without any prescription, through patient self-demand or pharmacist recommendation, so the law is inconsistently enforced on the ground.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Because the law clearly requires a prescription, travelers assume it is enforced the way it would be in a country with strict pharmacy oversight.

dead_ends.action: Self-diagnose and buy an antibiotic over the counter based on symptoms alone because pharmacies will sell it without a prescription
dead_ends.why_fails: Pharmacy staff dispensing without a prescription are not diagnosing the underlying illness; DRAP's 2024 advisory was issued specifically because unsupervised self-medication is driving antimicrobial resistance, so the drug obtained this way may be the wrong antibiotic, wrong dose, or unnecessary for a viral illness.

workarounds.action: See a registered doctor for a proper diagnosis and prescription when possible
workarounds.how: Use a clinic, hospital OPD, or telemedicine consultation with a PMDC-registered doctor to get an accurate diagnosis before taking an antibiotic, rather than relying on a pharmacist's guess.

workarounds.action: If buying over the counter is unavoidable, treat it as a stopgap and confirm the drug/dose with a pharmacist or doctor as soon as possible
workarounds.how: Do not assume OTC availability means the drug is appropriate; follow up with a medical professional to confirm the choice and complete course.
workarounds.condition: Applies when no doctor is reachable in the short term.
